subject.title: Gateway protocol: support attachment references in addition to inline Base64 attachments

question: Should OpenClaw standardize Gateway-owned staged asset handles for `chat.send`, expose a namespaced plugin resolver contract for external object stores, or keep the protocol inline-only?
rationale: The code can add a union mechanically, but only maintainers can choose the durable ownership and trust boundary shared by WebChat, native clients, third-party clients, plugins, and remote Gateways.

options.title: Gateway-owned asset handles
options.body: Add an authenticated upload or chunk-staging surface and let `chat.send` reference only opaque assets owned and validated by the receiving Gateway.

options.title: Namespaced resolver contract
options.body: Let trusted plugins register reference namespaces and resolvers, accepting greater API and security complexity to support external object stores directly.

options.title: Retain inline transport
options.body: Keep Base64 attachments as the only `chat.send` contract and document payload limits rather than expanding the protocol and storage lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Gateway-owned asset handles
recommendation.body: Add an authenticated upload or chunk-staging surface and let `chat.send` reference only opaque assets owned and validated by the receiving Gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans the public Gateway contract, core storage ownership, security posture, and all first-party clients, matching the project-level gateway decision role.
